pr_body:
This change allows test writers to set a MinBootstrapVersion. This option will tell to the mixed version framework to not generate any plans that create a cluster on any versions older than MinBootstrapVersion.

With this new option, the `http-register-routes/mixed-versions` test now sets the MinBootstrapVersion to 24.2, the oldest release that has the fix contained in https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/138342.

Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/138861
Release note: none

This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/142211)

missing a `./dev gen` to fix build file:
```
+++ b/pkg/cmd/roachtest/roachtestutil/mixedversion/BUILD.bazel
@@ -71,6 +71,7 @@ go_test(
         "//pkg/testutils/release",
         "//pkg/util/intsets",
         "//pkg/util/randutil",
+        "//pkg/util/retry",
```
A nice to have would be to add a small section to the `/mixedversion/REAMDE.md` doc explaining that min bootstrap is different from min version, and what it does.

Fun failure on stress that suggests I broke something with the rng 🙃 :

```
=== RUN   Test_stepSelectorFilter/no_filter
    planner_test.go:622:
          Error Trace:  pkg/cmd/roachtest/roachtestutil/mixedversion/planner_test.go:622
          Error:        Object expected to be of type mixedversion.runHookStep, but was mixedversion.restartWithNewBinaryStep
          Test:         Test_stepSelectorFilter/no_filter
--- FAIL: Test_stepSelectorFilter/no_filter (0.01s)
```

Interestingly, this works fine locally when I run `./dev test pkg/cmd/roachtest/roachtestutil/mixedversion --stress --count=50000` as well as `./dev test pkg/cmd/roachtest/roachtestutil/mixedversion --stress --race --count=10000`, but seems to fail pretty consistently on CI

My current (wild) guess is it's something to do with the fact unit tests now use `clusterupgrade.CurrentVersion()` and this somehow behaves different under CI. Sorry in advance for the large amounts of force pushing as I try to debug with CI :)

> Test_stepSelectorFilter/no_filter

@DarrylWong this baked my noodle for a while :)

But it seems it's **test execution order** that is causing a different scenario (I think a normal stress always runs it in the same order?).

You can easily **reproduce** the failure with a Test Order Seed:

`./dev test pkg/cmd/roachtest/roachtestutil/mixedversion --ignore-cache --test-args '-test.shuffle=5'`

or

`_bazel/bin/pkg/cmd/roachtest/roachtestutil/mixedversion/mixedversion_test_/mixedversion_test -test.run=. -test.v -test.shuffle=5`

There's some randomization somewhere that is dependent on test order (probably package global); and we should probably also fix that, I'm curious where it is, but haven't been able to track it down yet.

I noted CI has:
```
	planner_test.go:622: Seed:               12345
	Upgrades:           v24.1.1 → v24.2.2 → v24.3.0 → <current>
```

and all my `local` / `gce_worker` builds had:
```
    planner_test.go:622: Seed:               12345
    Upgrades:           v23.1.17 → v23.2.4 → v24.1.1 → <current>
```

which made me wonder how the same seed produced two different `Upgrades`.

Okay well that was pretty easy to figure out thanks to Herko's repro.

In `withTestBuildVersion` which is used to configure the build version for a test, we correctly try and reset the build version once we're done:

```
return func() { clusterupgrade.TestBuildVersion = nil }
```

Unfortunately we reset it to `nil` (which means to use the build version of the crdb binary, `25.2`) instead of setting it back to our default "test build version" (`24.2`). So if `Test_stepSelectorFilter` is run before any test that calls `withTestBuildVersion`, it will create an upgrade plan to `24.2`, otherwise it will create a plan to `25.2`.

Another case of "i'm shocked this hasn't flaked until now" 😃
Browser + internet glitch says this PR is now twice approved 🙃

Smoke test here: https://teamcity.cockroachdb.com/buildConfiguration/Cockroach_Nightlies_RoachtestNightlyGceBazel/19115007?hideProblemsFromDependencies=false&hideTestsFromDependencies=false&expandBuildChangesSection=true&expandBuildTestsSection=true

acceptance failure is unrelated.

TFTRs!
